title: Bad Timezone
description: A dispatcher fat-fingers the timezone selector into something that isn't a real IANA name. The schema itself doesn't catch this — it's checked later, when the bucketing logic tries to actually use it.
successCondition: GET /api/reporting/summary as a dispatcher with timeZone set to a non-existent zone name (e.g. "Mars/Olympus_Mons") does not return a 200 with silently-wrong data — it either returns a 400/500 error response with a structured error.code, or (if the API instead falls back to a default) a follow-up request confirms the response's behavior is documented and deliberate, not silently corrupted.
hints: docs/api/reporting.md notes timezone validity is deferred to Intl itself and "caught in the service layer" — read apps/api/src/modules/reporting/bucketing.ts to see exactly what happens when Intl.DateTimeFormat is given a bad zone name, and assert on that actual behavior rather than assuming.
Compare against a request with a valid but unusual IANA name (e.g. "Pacific/Kiritimati") to confirm the failure is specific to invalid names, not timezones generally.
